lesson_content_what_is_forex:
Introduction

The foreign exchange market (Forex or FX) is the largest and most liquid financial market on Earth — with over $7.5 trillion traded every single day. Unlike stock markets, Forex has no central exchange and no physical location. It runs 24 hours a day, 5 days a week across Sydney, Tokyo, London, and New York.

Key Concept 1 — What Is Being Traded?

In Forex you are exchanging one currency for another. Currencies are traded in pairs such as EUR/USD or GBP/JPY. The price tells you how much of one currency you need to buy one unit of the other.

Key Concept 2 — Who Trades Forex?

  • 🏦 Central Banks — manage national reserves and monetary policy
  • 🏢 Commercial Banks — facilitate international trade
  • 📊 Hedge Funds — speculate for profit using large capital
  • 👤 Retail Traders (you) — trade via online brokers

Key Concept 3 — Why Trade Forex?

  • ✅ Highest liquidity — enter and exit positions instantly
  • ✅ Low barriers to entry — start with as little as $100
  • ✅ Trade both directions — profit when prices rise OR fall
  • ✅ Leverage — control large positions with a small deposit
  • ✅ 24/5 access — trade any time during the week

Key Concept 4 — The Four Trading Sessions

SessionHours (UTC)Key Pairs
Sydney10pm – 7amAUD/USD
Tokyo12am – 9amUSD/JPY
London8am – 5pmEUR/USD, GBP/USD
New York1pm – 10pmUSD/CAD
💡 The London–New York overlap (1pm–5pm UTC) is the most volatile and liquid window.

Key Concept 5 — Risk Warning

Forex trading carries significant risk. Leverage amplifies both profits and losses. Never trade money you cannot afford to lose. Always start on a demo account.

Quick Quiz

Q1: Approximate daily Forex trading volume?

A) $250 billion

B) $7.5 trillion ✅

C) $500 million

Q2: Which session overlap has the highest liquidity?

A) Tokyo–Sydney

B) London–New York ✅

C) Sydney–Tokyo

Q3: In Forex you can profit ONLY when prices go up. True or False?

A) True

B) False — you can profit in both directions ✅
lesson_content_currency_pairs:
Introduction

In Forex you always trade a currency pair — simultaneously buying one currency and selling another. Understanding pairs is the foundation of everything in Forex.

Key Concept 1 — Anatomy of a Currency Pair

Every pair has two parts:

  • Base Currency — the first (what you are buying)
  • Quote Currency — the second (what you are selling)

Example: EUR/USD = 1.0850 — it costs $1.0850 to buy exactly €1.00.

💡 If EUR/USD rises from 1.0850 to 1.0900, the Euro got stronger — a bullish move.

Key Concept 2 — The Four Categories of Pairs

CategoryExamplesCharacteristics
MajorsEUR/USD, GBP/USD, USD/JPYHighest liquidity, tightest spreads
MinorsEUR/GBP, GBP/JPYGood liquidity, no USD
ExoticsUSD/TRY, USD/NGNLower liquidity, wider spreads
MetalsXAU/USD (Gold)Highly volatile, safe-haven

Key Concept 3 — Bid, Ask, and the Spread

  • Bid — the price the broker buys from you (your sell price)
  • Ask — the price the broker sells to you (your buy price)

The difference is the Spread — the broker's fee. EUR/USD typically: 0.5–2 pips. Exotics: 20–50 pips.

💡 Always enter a BUY at the Ask and exit at the Bid. The spread is the cost on every trade.

Key Concept 4 — Correlation Between Pairs

  • EUR/USD and GBP/USD usually move together (~80% positive correlation)
  • EUR/USD and USD/CHF usually move opposite (~-90% negative correlation)
  • USD/JPY and XAU/USD often move opposite (risk sentiment)

Key Concept 5 — Reading a Quote

On any trading platform: EUR/USD 1.08520 / 1.08534

  • 1.08520 = Bid (sell here)
  • 1.08534 = Ask (buy here)
  • Spread = 1.4 pips

Quick Quiz

Q1: In EUR/USD, which is the BASE currency?

A) USD

B) EUR ✅

C) Both equally

Q2: The SPREAD is best described as:

A) Profit on a trade

B) Difference between Bid and Ask price ✅

C) Overnight swap fee

Q3: Which pair category has the WIDEST spreads?

A) Majors

B) Minors

C) Exotics ✅
lesson_content_what_is_pip:
Pips, Lots, and Position Sizing

A pip (Percentage in Point) is the smallest standard price movement in forex. For most pairs, 1 pip = 0.0001.

Example

If EUR/USD moves from 1.0850 → 1.0860, that's a 10 pip move.

Lot Sizes

  • Standard Lot = 100,000 units → 1 pip = $10
  • Mini Lot = 10,000 units → 1 pip = $1
  • Micro Lot = 1,000 units → 1 pip = $0.10

Why Pips Matter

Pips are how traders measure profit and loss. If you buy 1 standard lot of EUR/USD and it moves 50 pips in your favor, you made $500.

💡 Key Takeaway: Master pip calculation before risking real money. Always know your pip value before entering a trade.
lesson_content_support_resistance:
Support and Resistance — The Foundation of Technical Analysis

Support is a price level where buying pressure is strong enough to prevent the price from falling further. Resistance is where selling pressure prevents the price from rising further.

How to Identify Key Levels

  • Look for price areas where the market has reversed multiple times
  • Round numbers (1.1000, 1.0500) often act as psychological S/R
  • Previous highs and lows are natural S/R zones

The Role Reversal Concept

When price breaks through a resistance level, that level often becomes new support — and vice versa. This is called role reversal and is one of the most powerful concepts in trading.

💡 Key Takeaway: Support and resistance are zones, not exact lines. Always look for confluence — multiple reasons for price to react at a level.
lesson_content_candlesticks:
Reading Candlestick Patterns

Candlesticks show four key prices: Open, High, Low, Close. The body shows the range between open and close. The wicks show the extremes.

Key Reversal Patterns

  • 🕯️ Doji — Open ≈ Close. Market indecision. Watch for direction after.
  • 🔨 Hammer — Long lower wick at support. Bullish reversal signal.
  • ⭐ Shooting Star — Long upper wick at resistance. Bearish reversal signal.
  • 🌙 Engulfing — One candle completely engulfs the previous. Strong reversal.

How to Use Them

Never trade a candlestick pattern in isolation. Always confirm with:

  • Key support/resistance level
  • Trend direction
  • Volume or momentum indicator
💡 Key Takeaway: Candlestick patterns are clues, not guarantees. Use them as confirmation, not as standalone signals.
lesson_content_trend_lines:
Trend Lines and Market Structure

The most fundamental concept in trading: the trend is your friend. Understanding market structure tells you whether to look for buys, sells, or to stay out.

Market Structure

  • 📈 Uptrend = Higher Highs (HH) + Higher Lows (HL)
  • 📉 Downtrend = Lower Highs (LH) + Lower Lows (LL)
  • ↔️ Ranging = Price bouncing between two levels

Drawing Trend Lines

In an uptrend, connect the higher lows. In a downtrend, connect the lower highs. A break of the trend line signals a potential reversal.

Trading With the Trend

Always trade in the direction of the higher timeframe trend. If the daily chart is bullish, look for buy setups on the 1-hour chart.

💡 Key Takeaway: Identify the trend on a higher timeframe first, then drop to a lower timeframe to find your entry. This is called top-down analysis.

lesson_content_read_chart:
Introduction

A price chart is your window into the market. Every decision you make will be influenced by what you see on a chart. Before you can analyse markets, spot setups, or manage trades, you need to understand how to read what the chart is telling you.

Key Concept 1 — The Three Chart Types

  • 📊 Line Chart — plots only the closing price. Simple but hides detail.
  • 📉 Bar Chart (OHLC) — shows Open, High, Low, Close as vertical bars.
  • 🕯️ Candlestick Chart — same OHLC data in a visual, easy-to-read format. Used exclusively at 27pips.
💡 Always use candlestick charts — the industry standard for retail traders.

Key Concept 2 — Anatomy of a Candlestick

Each candle represents one time period and shows four prices: Open, Close, High, Low.

ColourMeaningClose vs Open
🟢 Green (Bullish)Buyers wonClose higher than Open
🔴 Red (Bearish)Sellers wonClose lower than Open

Key Concept 3 — Timeframes

  • ⚡ M1, M5, M15 — Scalping (very short-term, very noisy)
  • 📈 H1, H4 — Day trading and swing trading (most popular)
  • 📅 Daily (D1) — Clearest signals, swing trading
  • 🗓️ Weekly (W1) — Long-term trend identification
💡 Always check the Daily or Weekly chart first to find the dominant trend, then drop to H1/H4 for your entry. This is Top-Down Analysis.

Key Concept 4 — Support and Resistance on a Chart

Train your eye to spot support (price floors) and resistance (price ceilings):

  • Areas where price has reversed multiple times
  • Round numbers (1.1000, 1.0500) act as magnets
  • Previous swing highs become resistance; lows become support

Key Concept 5 — Trend Recognition in 10 Seconds

  • 📈 Higher Highs + Higher Lows = Uptrend (look for buys)
  • 📉 Lower Highs + Lower Lows = Downtrend (look for sells)
  • ↔️ No clear direction = Range (wait for a breakout)
💡 Never fight a strong trend. Wait for pullbacks in the trend direction.

Quick Quiz

Q1: A GREEN candlestick means the Close is HIGHER than the Open.

A) False

B) True ✅

Q2: To identify the dominant trend, check which timeframe FIRST?

A) M5 (5-minute)

B) Daily or Weekly chart ✅

C) M15 (15-minute)

Q3: Higher Highs and Higher Lows describe which market condition?

A) Downtrend

B) Ranging market

C) Uptrend ✅
